questions.prompt:
Part (a): Calculate the area of \(\mathbf r(u,v)=(13u,14v,0)\) on \(0\le u,v\le1\).
Part (b): Prove that swapping the parameters of a surface reverses its oriented normal.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[\mathbf r_u=(13,0,0),\quad\mathbf r_v=(0,14,0),\quad|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v|=182.\]
Thus \(A=\int_0^1\int_0^1182\,du\,dv\).
Final answer: The area is \(182\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
The original oriented area vector is \(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\). After swapping \(u,v\), it becomes
\[\mathbf r_v\times\mathbf r_u=-(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v).\]
Final answer: Parameter swapping reverses orientation.

Part (b): Prove that the flux through a surface changes sign when its orientation is reversed.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[\mathbf r_u=(15,0,0),\quad\mathbf r_v=(0,16,0),\quad|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v|=240.\]

Final answer: The area is \(240\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Orientation reversal replaces \(\mathbf n\) by \(-\mathbf n\), so

Final answer: Reversing orientation negates the flux.
